questions.stem: The length of time, $L$ hours, that a phone will work before it needs charging is normally distributed with a mean of 100 hours and a standard deviation of 15 hours.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: attempting to standardise with 127, 100 and 15. Allow $\pm$
A1: for $Z>1.8$. Allow a diagram but must have 1.8 and correct area indicated. Must have the $Z$ so $\mathrm{P}(L>127)$ with or without a diagram is insufficient. May be implied by 0.0359
A1: for awrt 0.0359 (calc. gives 0.035930266...). Correct answer only 3/3. M1A0A1 not possible.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\frac{127-100}{15}$ M1
- So $\mathrm{P}(L>127)=\mathrm{P}(Z>1.8)$ or $1-\mathrm{P}(Z<1.8)$ o.e. A1
$=1-0.9641=\mathbf{0.0359}$ (awrt $\mathbf{0.0359}$) A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the value of $d$ such that $\mathrm{P}(L<d)=0.10$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for an attempt to standardise with 100 and 15 and set $=\pm$ any $z$ value ($|z|>1$)
B1: for $z=\pm1.2816$ (or better) seen anywhere [May be implied by 80.776(72...) or better seen]
A1: for awrt 80.8 (can be scored for using 1.28 but then they get M1B0A1). The 80.8 must follow from correct working.
If answer is awrt 80.8 and awrt 80.777 or 80.776... or better seen then award M1B1A1
If answer is awrt 80.8 or 80.77 then award M1B0A1 (unless of course $z=1.2816$ is seen)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\frac{d-100}{15}=-1.2816$ (Calculator gives $-1.2815515\ldots$) M1, B1
- $d=80.776$ (awrt $\mathbf{80.8}$) A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Alice is about to go on a 6 hour journey.
Given that it is 127 hours since Alice last charged her phone,
(c) find the probability that her phone will not need charging before her journey is completed.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Require $\mathrm{P}(L>133 \mid L>127)$
M1: for clear indication of correct conditional probability or attempt at correct ratio. So clear attempt at $\frac{\mathrm{P}(L>133)}{\mathrm{P}(L>127)}$ is sufficient for the 1st M1
dM1: dependent on 1st M1 for $\mathrm{P}(L>133)$ leading to $\mathrm{P}(Z>2.2)$
$=\left[\frac{\mathrm{P}(L>133)}{\mathrm{P}(L>127)}\right]=\frac{\mathrm{P}(Z>2.2)}{\mathrm{P}(L>127)}=\left[\frac{1-0.9861}{1-0.9641}\right]=\frac{0.0139}{[0.0359]}$
A1: for 0.0139 or better seen coming from $\mathrm{P}(Z>2.20)$. Dependent on both Ms
A1: for awrt 0.39. Both Ms required
S.C.: An attempt at $\mathrm{P}(L<133\mid L>127)$ that leads to awrt 0.61 (M0M1A0A0)
ALT: If they assume Alice did not check that the phone was working you may see: $[\mathrm{P}(L<127).0]+\mathrm{P}(L>127).\mathrm{P}(L>133\mid L>127)$ Provided the conditional probability is seen as part of this calculation the 1st M1 can be scored and their final answer will be 0.0139(4/4). An answer of 0.0139 without sight of the conditional probability is 0/4.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $=0.3871\ldots$ = awrt $\mathbf{0.39}$ A1

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for attempt to use the addition rule. Correct substitution i.e. correct expression seen: $\mathrm{P}(A \cup B)=0.35+0.45-0.13$ or $0.22+0.13+0.32$
A1: for 0.67 only. Correct answer only scores 2/2
Official notes (completeness pass):
- NB May see Venn diagram for $A$ and $B$ only used for (a) and (b) but M marks are awarded for correct expressions only. No ft from an incorrect diagram for M marks.

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for a correct ratio of probabilities or a correct formula and at least one correct prob: $\mathrm{P}(A' \mid B')=\frac{\mathrm{P}(A' \cap B')}{\mathrm{P}(B')}$ or $\frac{0.33}{0.55}$. For a correct formula allow "$1-$their(a)" instead of 0.33 but not for correct ratio case. Do not award for assuming independence i.e. $\frac{\mathrm{P}(A' \cap B')}{\mathrm{P}(B')}=\frac{0.65\times0.55}{0.55}$ is M0. M0 if num>denom
A1: for $\frac{3}{5}$ or 0.6 or any exact equivalent.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $=\frac{3}{5}$ or 0.6 A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The event $C$ has $\mathrm{P}(C)=0.20$
The events $A$ and $C$ are mutually exclusive and the events $B$ and $C$ are independent.
(c) Find $\mathrm{P}(B \cap C)$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for correct expression $\mathrm{P}(B \cap C)=0.45\times 0.2$. Need correct values for $\mathrm{P}(B)$ and $\mathrm{P}(C)$ seen.
A1: for 0.09 or any exact equivalent. Correct answer only is 2/2

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Draw a Venn diagram to illustrate the events $A$, $B$ and $C$ and the probabilities for each region.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
No labels $A$, $B$, $C$ in (d) loses 1st B1 but can score the other 3 by implication
B1: for box with $B$ intersecting $A$ and $C$ but $C$ not intersecting $A$. No box is B0
B1ft: for 0.13 and their 0.09 in correct places. [ft $\mathrm{P}(B \cap C)$ from (c)]
B1: for any 2 of 0.22, $\underline{0.22}$, 0.11 and 0.23 correct
B1: for all 4 values correct
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Allow 1st B1 for 3 intersecting circles in a box with zeros in the regions for $A\cap C$. Do not accept "blank" for zero

parts.label: e
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for a correct expression or follow through from their Venn diagram: $\mathrm{P}(B \cup C)'=0.22+\underline{0.22}$ or $1-[0.56]$ or $1-[0.13+0.23+0.09+0.11]$ o.e.
A1: for 0.44 only. Correct answer only is 2/2
NB $\mathrm{P}(B')\times \mathrm{P}(C')=0.55\times 0.8$ is OK. Do not ft "blank" for zero and M0 for negative probs.
